method.type: direct proof of feasibility equivalence plus adversarial proof review; no experiment

mathematical_claim: For every finite metric and injective terminal labeling, OPT_(G,k)(mu,tau) is finite if and only if G has a terminal Multiway Cut of size at most k. This eliminates the infeasible-instance quotient pathology from feasible lower-bound work. No credible feasible family forcing a superlinear contraction-only quotient survived the joint-contraction review in this cycle.
assumptions: The graph is finite and undirected; parallel edges count separately and loops contribute no crossings or cost.
A terminal Multiway Cut leaves at most one terminal per connected component.
Terminal labels are injective, while nonterminals may use any label in the finite metric domain.
The contraction-only model and arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifier model remain distinct.
No computational experiment or new budget was used.
verified_steps: The crossing edges of any feasible extension form a terminal Multiway Cut of size at most k.
Given any terminal Multiway Cut of size at most k, labeling each post-cut component constantly gives a finite-cost extension with at most k crossings.
The equivalence is metric-independent and labeling-independent under terminal injectivity.
An infeasible-instance quotient cannot be used as evidence for a feasible lower bound.
The pairwise-signature route supplies no joint-contraction hitting-set theorem and cannot be promoted to a superlinear bound.
The next feasible research question is a series-parallel interface characterization beyond cactus.
gaps: The existence or impossibility of a feasible superlinear contraction-only lower bound remains open.
No exact series-parallel interface composition lemma has yet been proved.
No result transfers to arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifiers.

counterexamples.claim_refuted: An infeasible pure quotient with arbitrarily many forced edges can establish a feasible contraction-only lower bound.
counterexamples.counterexample: The feasibility equivalence shows every such witness has Multiway Cut optimum greater than k and is outside the feasible-instance target.

counterexamples.claim_refuted: Pairwise low-cut or metric signatures alone imply a superlinear joint-contraction lower bound.
counterexamples.counterexample: Joint contractions may preserve many signatures with one quotient structure; no hitting-set implication follows without an additional lemma.

uncertainty: The blocked route is a construction failure, not a theorem ruling out all feasible superlinear families.
The series-parallel alternative is a proof program, not an established bound.
The source's full sparsifier model remains broader than contraction-only quotients.

proof_status.scope: Feasibility equivalence is complete; the attempted feasible superlinear route is blocked by the absence of a joint-contraction hitting-set lemma.
excluded_claims: No feasible superlinear or k^(Omega(s)) lower bound is claimed.
No arbitrary-sparsifier lower bound is claimed.
